source: Manual entry 2026-08-07 from the 3ie Replication Paper 21 PDF (Reimão 2019, doi:10.23846/RPS0021), Table 4 (pure replication of original Table VII), using the public World Bank Microdata Library household survey data.
explanation: Pure replication, Table 4 col 2 (pure replication of original Table VII): original beta = -0.079 (cluster-robust SE 0.022), N = 2,084; replication beta = -0.076 (SE 0.021), N = 2,076; both significant at p<0.01 (stars), Westfall-Young adjusted p = 0.0086 (footnote 12). Coefficients are OLS linear-probability estimates with SEs clustered at the enumeration-area level; the paper reports significance stars only, so the 95% CIs here are computed as beta +/- 1.96*SE and the replication p-value is the Westfall-Young multiplicity-adjusted p from footnote 12. The replication had access only to the public World Bank household survey data (~10 fewer observations than the original); teacher-reported enrollment, school ledger and test score data were not public, so the original's headline CCT-vs-UCT contrast on objective schooling outcomes was not testable in the pure replication (the push-button replication with the original authors' own files reproduced the full paper, 'complete with minor differences'). The replicator: 'The portions that are replicable produce results that are largely the same as those presented in the original paper.'

source: Manual entry 2026-08-07 from the 3ie Replication Paper 26 PDF (Prasad, Djimeu, Korte & Glandon 2022, doi:10.23846/RPS0026), Table 2 cont'd (adjusted HIV incidence rates).
explanation: Arm A (full PopART with universal ART) vs Arm C (standard of care), Table 2 cont'd: original aRR = 0.93 (95% CI 0.74-1.18, p = 0.51); replication aRR = 1.11 (95% CI 0.86-1.44, p = 0.41) - both null, so the original's headline null conclusion is unchanged (coded success, matching the RPS0025/TasP precedent for a confirmed null). n is the baseline population cohort of the two arms (Arm A 12,671 + Arm C 12,399). This is an internal replication (reanalysis of the original trial data). Effect is the adjusted HIV incidence rate ratio over months 12-36. The push-button replication with the original code and data reproduced the original Tables 1-2 and Figures 2-3 exactly. The pure replication could not reproduce the original two-stage approach across 20 hot-deck-imputed datasets (insufficient documentation of the authors' custom R functions) and instead fit a single individual-level Poisson model adjusting for triplet, age, sex and baseline HIV prevalence, which is why the point estimates differ.
